whatThePageStates: This page is the published catalogue of the finding types that Amazon GuardDuty AI Protection can generate. A short introduction says GuardDuty analyzes AWS CloudTrail management events and data events from Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, that the Resource type for all of these findings is AccessKey, and which findings carry resource.modelDetails versus resource.bedrockGuardrailDetails. A Topics list names three finding types, and each then gets its own section with a one-sentence description heading, a Default severity line, a Feature line, an explanation of the detection logic, a MITRE ATLAS mapping, and remediation advice. The only table on the page describes the four fields of the resource.bedrockGuardrailDetails object for one finding, not coverage. The page makes no not-supported statement of any kind: it lists what exists and is silent about everything else.

features.statuses: 3 published finding types, all present-and-supported; 0 stated as not supported; 0 partial. 3 Topics bullets = 3 finding-name H2 sections (excluding the trailing 'See also' H2) = 3 description H3s = 3 'Default severity' lines = 3 'Feature: AI Protection' lines; 3=3=3=3=3. The names are Impact:IAMUser/AnomalousModelInvocation, Impact:IAMUser/CostHarvesting, Impact:IAMUser/PromptInjection.Direct. A finding type having a section on this page IS the coverage claim; there is no Yes/No column, no 'isn't available' sentence, and no exclusion note anywhere on the page, so no negative status can be read from it.
features.scope: Applicability notes per finding, stated in prose, not a second enumerated dimension: AnomalousModelInvocation and CostHarvesting apply to both Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI model invocations, while PromptInjection.Direct applies only to Amazon Bedrock workloads that use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with a prompt attack content filter. Every finding also carries Default severity Low and Feature 'AI Protection'. There is no per-Region, per-partition, per-plan or per-detector-version scope on this page.
features.reasoning: The page enumerates named GuardDuty finding-type identifiers, a list GuardDuty publishes about itself, so the axis is findingType and the kind is catalogue. The unit of claim is one finding type, because that is the granularity at which the page gives a name, a severity, a feature label and a detection description. The 3 finding types appear in five independent places on the page and agree at 3 each way, so there is no row-versus-target gap and no collapse to record. Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI are named as the analyzed sources, but they are never enumerated as a matrix with statuses, so 'service' is not a defensible second axis here.

shouldNotExtract: The 4-row resource.bedrockGuardrailDetails field table (guardrails, guardrailAction, guardrailSource, contentPolicyFilters) — it is a finding-JSON schema description, not coverage. The IAM action bullet lists in the remediation sections (8 model invocation APIs, repeated under two findings, 16 bullets in total) — these are hardening advice, not covered API operations. The 4 baseline-feature bullets under AnomalousModelInvocation (API called, model invoked, source IP/ASN, user agent) — profiling inputs, not an axis. The 'Default severity: Low' and 'Feature: AI Protection' lines — labels, not statuses. The MITRE ATLAS technique links (AML.T0040, AML.T0034, AML.T0051) — a mapping to an external framework, not a coverage enumeration. All outbound links to the Bedrock, SageMaker AI, Organizations, Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection guides. And the 'See also' section with the Agent Toolkit for AWS / aws agent-toolkit search-skills AI-coding-assistant boilerplate, which is on every page and carries no coverage.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never names a Region, a partition, or a Region-availability caveat; any per-Region figure taken from this page is fabricated. SERVICE: no enumeration and no statuses. Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI are named in prose as the sources GuardDuty analyzes and as the applicability of individual findings, but the page does not present a service list with Yes/No, so it supports a statement about which two AI services these three findings apply to and nothing more. RESOURCE TYPE: exactly one value is stated — the Resource type for all three findings is AccessKey — which is a constant, not an enumerated axis; the modelDetails prose additionally names Bedrock foundation models, inference profiles, provisioned/custom/imported model ARNs, Marketplace endpoints, prompt resources and SageMaker AI endpoint names as things the finding reports on, but these are JSON field contents, not a covered-resource-type matrix.
trap: The most likely misparse is double counting the finding types: the 3 Topics bullets and the 3 finding H2 headings are the same 3 items, so a parser that harvests both reports 6. The next most likely error is counting all H2 headings and picking up the trailing 'See also' section as a fourth finding type. Runners-up: harvesting the 4-row bedrockGuardrailDetails field table as a coverage table (it is finding JSON schema); harvesting the remediation bullet lists of IAM actions as covered apiOperations (8 per list, 16 total, all duplicates of each other); reading 'Default severity: Low' as a coverage status or as a Partial; and inferring a 'not supported' anywhere — the page states no negatives at all, so a No count from this page is invented.
